I cannot understand the output or see anything which I can reproduce. I'm fairly confident that the PR itself wouldn't cause any problems with leanblueprint but I tried rerunning the job and it failed again. I guess I can just keep trying?
I remember in another thread it was explained this was a CI cache problem. I haven't tried it myself, but I heard there is a button to clear ci cache to resolve this

I have the same error again. (error code: 4294967294), see the logs above).

Right now CI seems to have about a 30% chance of succeeding if it involved having to make the docs, which happens iff it's a commit to main (i.e. a merge commit). Furthermore it spends over 2.5 hours churning before it fails. This is a ridiculous waste of CPU cycles.

I will now do the only thing I know how to do, which is to go to the repo on github, then actions tab, then caches, then clear all the caches, and then retry. But even that sometimes fails.

My conclusion is that doc-gen is not fit for purpose for FLT right now. The only changes I am making to FLT Lean code right now is stuff like technical debt reduction; I am not actively working on the development of any new theory, all my time is going into writing FLT lectures. It is extremely frustrating to have constant red x's in CI and it is also frustrating to have to wait for 159 minutes to get them; it hugely slows down development because I don't like merging PR n+1 until I see the green tick in PR n, and I want to make PRs which do things like removal of set_option backward stuff or bumping mathlib but today, for example, I have had a 2.5 hour CI failure twice on one commit which just adds docstrings, so there has been a 7.5 hour freeze on PR merging.
@Kevin Buzzard FLT#947 should solve your problems.

Re "several other projects which I've never heard of ran into the same problem and solved it but I had no idea about this" -- is there some kind of "downstream of mathlib self help club" where information like this gets circulated? I ran into a discussion on zulip about another downstream project with the same problem and the conclusion was "just keep clearing cache" so I started doing that about a week ago and when even that started failing I just decided to comment everything out and whinge here because I don't really want to wait 2.5 hours on a dice-roll. In fact to be honest I don't want to wait 2.5 hours full stop. Also there was a sharp increase in time from 1.25 hours to 2.5 hours recently. I'm wondering whether a better solution is "make the docs when I'm asleep" as opposed to "make the docs every time I push to main"

Kevin Buzzard said:

Re "several other projects which I've never heard of ran into the same problem and solved it but I had no idea about this" -- is there some kind of "downstream of mathlib self help club" where information like this gets circulated?

There is the #ecosystem infrastructure channel, but it's not being used very much yet. Maybe we should encourage all downstream projects to post their CI problems there?
I would love to adopt that policy! I really don't like posting CI whinges in this channel.
